newsitem.title: USA: Apache presses Amoco for talks on assets.
newsitem.headline: Apache presses Amoco for talks on assets.

text.p: Apache Corp is eyeing Midwest U.S. oil and gas assets put up for sale by Amoco Corp this week but refuses to enter into an auction set up by the major oil company, Apache executives said Thursday.
The Houston-based independent pressed Amoco to consider a negotiated sale of its Oklahoma and Gulf Coast assets, which would fit neatly with Apache's core operations, a company spokesman said.
"We're a logical buyer and we want to do a negotiated transaction," Apache spokesman Tony Lentini said. "But if they do an auction, we don't want to play."

Amoco on Monday said it retained investment banking firm Morgan Stanley to manage an auction of 15 percent of its U.S. oil and gas properties. Analysts said the assets could fetch between $2 billion and $3 billion.
"Apache has shown an interest in the properties as have other companies," an Amoco spokesman said. "Morgan Stanley has already received a large number of inquiries."
Apache Chairman Raymond Plank said his company could lead a consortium to buy the entire package of assets if Chicago-based Amoco would scrap the auction plans and enter into a negotiated deal.

Apache has said it has the financial capacity to do about $500 million in acquisitions without taking on too much debt or having to issue shares. But the company has traditionally refused to bid in open auctions, favoring negotiated deals.
